readMe: ONE ARTIFACT, TWO CONSUMERS. The cloud coordinator reads this to know what has
been settled; the local sim session reads it to know what to run next.
`bin/make-promotion-batch.js` turns it into the next batch's spec files, so
'what should the PC run next?' is a command and not a judgement call.
THE ONE RULE THIS LEDGER EXISTS TO ENFORCE: a deterministic probe is NECESSARY
AND NEVER SUFFICIENT. CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED passed its deterministic ship gate
outright (fatal stagings 41 -> 0) and then lost snake6 1.00 -> 0.15 live, through
exhaustion — a travel-economy channel the probe does not measure. Only a live
paired sweep, with a concurrent verified null and a VERIFIED ENGAGED treatment
arm, may write a live status.

statusLadder: dark -> probe-passed  : a deterministic probe cleared its gate. Goes no further.
probe-passed -> live-* : only a live paired sweep with a verified concurrent null.
supported -> promoted  : the default flip was actually made; `promotedBy` names the commit.
frozen                 : re-opened by a MECHANISM CLAIM only, never by a p-value.
explorationSliceRule: A promoted or supported flag keeps ~10% of its cells running the OPPOSITE branch,
forever. Today's policy selects tomorrow's corpus, so a cell that turned a flag on
will otherwise never generate the data by which it could be turned back off.
powerArithmetic: A block is one seed through every cyclic seat rotation (3 games on a 3-team board).
Placement: 80% power at MDE 0.25 needs ~58 blocks on the pooled stratum, 8 on the
tightest (mix23 alone); MDE 0.10 needs 362-1,447. That is 360-1,000+ games per cell
PER ARM. Mechanism metrics move at n~8 blocks and are 5-25x outside the null band.
So: refit on mechanism, describe placement, and refuse a placement verdict from a
cell whose blocksHad < blocksNeeded. (A3 memo section 4.1.)
retiredCounters: plansEvaluated and boundsInversions are RETIRED as verdict-bearing metrics on any
live arm: at any budget they are dominated by how much CPU the process got. They
carry a verdict ONLY under a fixed-tick StepClock A/A, where the arms consume
identical work by construction. They are still reported, because they diagnose a
armEngagementRule: A live measurement must carry armEngagementVerified. `false` records the row and
moves nothing: a null from an arm that never ran is a different finding from a null
from an arm that ran and did not help. P5 is the standing exhibit — CENTAUR_WASM is
refused per partition, silently, whenever an input is not resident in linear memory.
CL7's mechanism report (TeamTurnResult.mechanism) is what makes the answer readable.
conventions.flagOrderIsPriority: THE FLAG ORDER IN THIS ARRAY IS THE BATCH ORDER. make-promotion-batch.js emits one experiment,per undecided flag in array order, and the batch is designed to be cut from the bottom when the,night is short. So reordering this array is how a priority is expressed, and it is the only,way the generator can hear one.,,BATCH-1 CHANGE: CENTAUR_WASM was moved from eighth to first among the undecided flags, ahead of,CENTAUR_EDGE_EV. P5R is the only scheduled experiment in batch 2 that CLOSES a standing anomaly,rather than opening a new question, the instrumentation that makes it readable landed in CL7,,and it carries a gate that makes a broken arm impossible to misreport as a null. — REVISED after LIVE-NULL-IS-TERMINAL closed: making live-null flags schedulable put CENTAUR_UNIT_FATALITY (P7F) ahead of CENTAUR_WASM (P5R) purely because of where it already sat in the array, which nobody decided. P5R stays FIRST — it is the only scheduled experiment that CLOSES a standing anomaly rather than opening a question, its instrumentation landed in CL7, and the COORDINATION note already told the local session it runs first. CENTAUR_UNIT_FATALITY is moved to just below CENTAUR_WASM so P7F is second: newly unblocked, and worth running, but not ahead of the experiment the batch was reprioritised around.
conventions.selectionField: `selection` says WHAT SELECTS THIS ARM TODAY, and the field exists because the answer stopped being "an environment variable" on 2026-08-29, when the owner had the feature-flag system torn out. A row keeps its FLAG NAME as its historical identity — every measurement under it was taken by that name — and `selection` is how the same arm is asked for now: a BotConfig field, a registry entry, or nothing at all where the flag turned out to be a CORRECTION and went in unconditionally. It moves no status and it is not a measurement.

vocabulary.ruling: OWNER RULING 20260830 (seventh message), recorded verbatim: "VOCABULARY BAN: 'dark', 'promoted/promotion' in owner-facing communication. Use: in-collection/selectable; validated; merged." And, on the architecture lane: "Say MERGE, never 'promote'; never 'dark'."
vocabulary.appliesTo: OWNER-FACING TEXT — this view's title, headings and badges, HANDOFF.md, the batch READMEs and every generated spec's prose.
vocabulary.doesNotApplyTo: INTERNAL IDENTIFIERS AND HISTORY. `promotion-ledger.json` is a filename; `lib/ledger.js`'s seven statuses (`dark`, `probe-passed`, `live-null`, `live-failed`, `supported`, `promoted`, `frozen`) are schema constants and row identities that every historical measurement is keyed on. Renaming them would rewrite the record to change a word, which is the opposite of what the ruling asks for. The machinery keeps its spelling; the human view translates.

translation.dark: merged, not selected — the code is in the tree and in its collection; nothing selects it yet
translation.probe-passed: probe only — deterministic evidence, no live race
translation.promoted: VALIDATED — raced live against a verified null, and selected by default
translation.promotion: validation (of evidence) / merge (of a branch) / selection (of a collection member)

mergeReading.whyItMayNotDecide: THE POWER RULE, and it was written into the spec before the batch ran. The pair's own measured dispersion puts a +/-0.10 sharePar read at about 73 BLOCKS PER BOARD; it shipped at 16. The observed half-widths (+/-0.5562 and +/-0.6263 on the two piece boards) confirm the prediction. A 16-block read may not decide this merge in EITHER direction, and the expensive mistake available here is reading three negative signs as evidence against the branch. THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE THE BRANCH DOES NOT HELP.
mergeReading.cheapestDecidableRead: ONE BOARD, NOT THREE, AND MAKE IT null-snake6. The blocks needed scale as (spread/target)^2, so the cost is set by the board's own dispersion and the three boards differ by a factor of six: null-snake6 floors at +/-0.1172 sharePar where headline-mix-king floors at +/-0.7413 and hazard-mix-king at +/-0.7893. Reading the merge on the two mix-king boards is what makes it a 1,314-game question. On null-snake6 alone, 73 blocks x 3 rotations x 2 arms = 438 games, plus an A/A null on that one cell at the same 73 blocks = 438 more: ABOUT 876 GAMES, roughly 5 hours on the box that did 2,472 in 13h22m. That is a THIRD of a night for a decidable read, against 2.9 nights for the three-board version. THE COST OF THE NARROWING, STATED: null-snake6 is the board where the branch is engaged but least loaded (388,220 cluster joints against 14.6M on headline-mix-king), so it is the board where the branch has least room to help — a null there does not license a null on the owner's board. It decides the merge only in the sense the branching policy asks for: does the search architecture pay for itself where it can be MEASURED. If the answer wanted is specifically about headline-mix-king, no affordable read exists at 16-block-class budgets and the honest move is to fix the board (raise the turn cap, which 85-100% cap rates say is needed anyway) before spending 2.9 nights on it.
mergeReading.alsoOwed: A SECOND BASELINE NULL. The A/A is two search-arch builds, by the kit convention that the null is the bundle the batch's arms share. So the BASELINE arm of P11a has no floor of its own, and the merge is being read against the challenger's noise. One extra A/A on the baseline bundle, on the same one cell, is the cheapest thing that closes it.

aaNull.why: LIKE WITH LIKE, AND IT IS THE SAME CONVENTION BATCH 1 USED. An A/A null is ONE bundle seated twice under two names (verify-null.js asserts an identical bundle SHA in both arms), so a cross-branch batch has to choose which bundle that is. The kit's convention is the bundle the batch's arms SHARE: batch 1 floored on `integrated` @ 66904d256103 because that build was the base arm of P1, P2 and P3, and then read P1 — integrated against perf-substrate, two different branches — against that floor. Batch 2's shared bundle is the search-architecture tip: it is the base arm of P7F, P9, P10, P12, P13, X9 and all three budget rungs, and one of P11's two arms. So the null is TWO SEARCH-ARCHITECTURE BUILDS.
aaNull.caveat: P11's baseline arm therefore has no floor of its own, and that asymmetry is named rather than hidden. It is the same asymmetry batch 1 accepted in the other direction. What makes it tolerable is what the floor is a fact ABOUT: the arms are launched at the same instant on the same boards with the same seeds and pair by gameId, so the paired delta's floor is dominated by the board and the box rather than by which of two builds of one repository generated the moves. A reader who wants that assumption tested should schedule a second null pair on the baseline bundle; it is the cheapest box time available and nothing here forbids it.

All three replays carry the same thrown decision: `BoundsInversionError: inverted ScoreBounds [lo, hi]: bank floor=B0 ceiling=B3 [bounds_inversion]`, with the floor above the ceiling by 0.0150, 0.0186 and 0.0196 on scores of 60.0, 251.3 and 149.8 — a RELATIVE gap of 1e-4 to 3e-4, three to four orders of magnitude below the quantities being compared. The categorical case — a DEAD ceiling under a finite floor — was fixed at 018d780 and that fix IS in this build; this is the residual NUMERICAL case, which wants a tolerance rather than a rewrite. CO-OCCURRENCE IS EXACT: over 5,520 lobster game-seats in this batch, `errors > 0`, `stagedNothing > 0` and `unstaged > 0` are true on the same three seats and on no others. A thrown decision emits nothing, so the cost in play is a FORFEITED TURN. ALL THREE ARE ON snake5-queen — the board this batch measures at 4.23 ms of enumeration per cluster joint, ten times any other board, i.e. the deepest accumulation chains in the batch. flags.verdict: DO NOT PROMOTE AS-IS — and the failure is SNAKE-DENSITY-DEPENDENT, not global. The deterministic gate passed and the live arm collapsed through a channel the gate does not measure. But the collapse is confined to the cells with few or no pieces: on null-snake6 the seed loses 1.00 -> 0.15, while on headline-mix-king placement is flat and two mechanism rows (finalMaterial +5.10 ✱, survived +0.146 ✱) run in its FAVOUR. Exhaustion inflation is present everywhere the snakes outnumber the pieces (x2.09 knight, x1.92 snake6, x1.19 mix-king) but only converts into a placement loss where there is no piece play to absorb it. The live reading is therefore not "the seed is a dead idea" but "the seed is admissible on some boards and ruinous on others, and nothing currently decides which board it is on". That points at a CONDITIONAL ADMISSION future — the same shape CENTAUR_STAGING_SAFETY already ships as `auto` after helping on piece boards and regressing on snake-only — and NOT at a retirement. The status stays live-failed and the ledger's own rule is why: a failure is undone by a root cause and a repaired arm, never by other cells declining to reproduce it. The piece-cell rows are the beginning of a root cause, not a second opinion. MACHINE INGEST, 20260829 — every transcribed number reproduces exactly, and the per-game rows sharpen the mechanism in three ways the aggregates could not. (1) EXHAUSTION IS A MINORITY OF THE DAMAGE: on null-snake6 the seed loses 260 units per 48 games against cl-off's 53 (x4.91), while replay-mined exhaustion goes 39 -> 75 (x1.92) — 185 of the 260 died of something the exhaustion headline does not name, which is a constraint on any root cause. (2) ON THE PIECE CELL IT CHANGES THE CAUSE MIX, NOT THE AMOUNT: snake5-knight total unit loss is flat (209 -> 215) while exhaustion doubles, and on headline-mix-king total loss FALLS (163 -> 137). That is the density-dependence stated mechanically. (3) IT IS A GRIND: median elimination turn 98 of a 120 cap, nothing before turn 30, and the losing games are the LONGER ones — so the `turns -9.98` row is a change in terminal KIND, not "dies earlier". Per block, all 16 snake6 seeds are hurt and none is spared, while snake5-knight is two populations cancelling (4 hurt, 8 flat, 4 helped). A root cause must predict which board is which. SOURCE-LEVEL RECONCILIATION, 20260829 — THE REJECT STANDS AND THE MECHANISM IS TWO CHANNELS, NOT ONE. Channel A is travel economy, and it is now sourced: the seed's objective is three repulsive de-confliction terms (same-cell contest, edge exchange, team-mate's body by tier) plus ONE weak attractor (follow-the-tail, capped at 0.06), and it contains NO food term and NO travel-cost term at all — so on a board where every unit is on a starvation clock, a purely spatial objective spends health, and exhaustion death here is death by movement cost (`turnEngine.ts:92`, `Game.ts:205`, food as the rescue). That channel is 16% of the damage, not 29% — and its stated MECHANISM is now falsified too: per-turn travel is EXACTLY 1.000 cells in both arms (delta +0.000, zero-width interval), because a snake moves one cell per turn by rule, so movement distance is a constant and cannot carry a health-cost difference. What the replays show instead is distance to nearest food +1.47 [+0.74, +2.20] ✱ under the seed: it starves units by keeping them FURTHER FROM FOOD, not by making them walk further. Channel B IS NOW MEASURED (20260829 replay re-mine, DEATH-CAUSE-SINGLE-KEY closed) AND IT IS THE MAJORITY: the full nine-kind `ClashKind` breakdown on null-snake6, subject team over 48 paired games, is contest 13 -> 70, edge 1 -> 9, bodyBlock 14 -> 72, wall 3 -> 58, self 15 -> 11, exhaustion 7 -> 40, total 53 -> 260. THE COLLISION CHANNEL {contest, edge, bodyBlock, wall, self} GOES 46 -> 220, WHICH IS +174 OF THE +207 EXCESS — 84% — AND EXHAUSTION IS +33, OR 16%. Three causes carry it in near-equal thirds (bodyBlock +58, contest +57, wall +55), each individually outside the floor; `self` is the only channel that improves. Per-game deltas blocked by seed: collision +3.6250 [+3.1906, +4.0594] ✱ against an A/A noise band of +0.0417 [-0.2752, +0.3585] — 10.1x the null's upper bound — and 16 of 16 seed blocks are hurt with none spared. cl-fatality, the order-preserving control, is +0.0000 [-0.3997, +0.3997] on the same channel, so the explosion is this seed and not any flag that touches the candidate set. The extraction is COMPLETE, not a sample: mined deaths equal units lost exactly for all four arms on all three cells, twelve checks and twelve exact matches. SO THE CL1 SHIP CRITERION IS FALSIFIED AS A LIVE PREDICTOR ON ITS OWN CHOSEN METRIC: offline it certified fatal stagings 41 -> 0 scattered, 64 -> 8 confronted and team-mate kills 25 -> 4; live, on that same collision channel, the seed turns 46 deaths into 220. Own-team bodyBlock kills go 0 -> 13. The offline safety result did not transfer, and the gap is 4.8x on the exact quantity the gate measured. AN ACCOUNTING CORRECTION COMES WITH IT: deaths-p7.json counts ALL THREE TEAMS and counts from `events.exhaustions[]`, and its 39 -> 75 was compared against a SUBJECT-ONLY unit-loss total of 53 -> 260, which is where '29% of the damage' came from. Like for like, subject-only, from `events.deaths`, exhaustion is 7 -> 40 — 15.4% of the seed's deaths and 15.9% of its excess. The prior figure overstated exhaustion's share by roughly 2x. PROCESS FINDING: the ship criterion gated on fatal stagings, a DIFFERENT death channel from the one that killed it, so any future seed/ordering flag must be gated on a CAUSE-OF-DEATH BREAKDOWN and not on stagings alone. PIECE-GATED ADMISSION — REJECTED, 20260829: DO NOT BUILD IT. The BOARD-LEVEL form of the conditional-admission reading above ("admit the seed only on piece-bearing boards") is falsified by a cell already in this batch. `snake5-knight` IS piece-bearing and would pass any board-level piece gate, and there the seed delivers exhaustion x2.09 (23 -> 48, the worst ratio in the batch), subject-team eliminations 1/48 -> 6/48, ratchet per decision +0.01026 ✱ (the largest in the batch — the seed's plan sticking), worstWallMs +4.29 ms ✱ — and score NULL (-0.0104 [-0.142, +0.121]). Full price, zero benefit. The piece-cell "win" on headline-mix-king does not carry the gate either: finalMaterial +5.10 [+0.44, +9.77] and survived +0.146 [+0.001, +0.290] are DIRECTION-ONLY — both lower bounds sit within 0.5 of zero, neither has a cell-local A/A floor, and that cell decorrelates completely under ZERO treatment (A/A 5 of 48 games identical in length, turn-correlation -0.193), so its per-game statistics carry far less information than n=48 suggests. The gate the mechanism implies is PER-UNIT, not per-board — the harm is a travel-economy cost borne by trail units while the benefit is de-confliction among units that contest cells, and the codebase already separates them — but the seed's ONLY positive term, follow-the-tail, is itself a trail-unit term, so a per-unit gate is a real design question with a plausible failure mode and not a one-liner. Order of work, REVISED 20260829 now that the re-mine is done and the damage is located: the travel-economy term in ψ drops from first to LAST — it addresses 16% of the deaths through a channel (movement distance) that does not vary — and a BOUNDARY / FORMATION term rises to first. The reason is the mechanism the replays actually show, which is neither spacing nor travel: controlled for survivorship (949 matched turn-pairs where both arms still hold all six units), the seed makes own-team head separation FALL 10.70 -> 6.51 (-3.97 ✱) and distance to nearest wall FALL 3.95 -> 2.00 (-1.80 ✱). The units CLUSTER and get PINNED AGAINST THE BOARD EDGE — the opposite of what three repulsive φ terms predict. THE SINGLE CLEANEST NUMBER IN THE PASS: the team's mean wall-distance drops below 2.0 by MEDIAN TURN 5 IN 48 OF 48 GAMES under the seed, against 5 of 48 ever under cl-off. Not a tendency, a structural outcome in every game. Everything else follows from that state without further assumption — wall deaths because the formation is on the boundary with nowhere to step (all 58 recorded at an off-board destination), bodyBlock and contest because six units packed into a small region share the same few free cells, exhaustion because a cornered team is systematically further from food, and the +103% plans-per-decision with 10x ratchet refusals because a search in a pocket with no legal improving move generates refinements to the deadline and refuses every one. A PER-UNIT GATE DOES NOT OBVIOUSLY ADDRESS PINNING, so it drops below a boundary/room term in ψ or an admission rule that refuses the seed when the team's own separation is falling. STATUS UNCHANGED BY THIS PARAGRAPH: live-failed stands, and the ledger's own rule is why — a failure is undone by a root cause and a repaired arm, never by a design idea.

flags.verdict: TERMINAL — CLOSED BY OWNER RULING, 20260829, and not by a measurement. The ruling, verbatim: "You should eliminate wasm. it's not worth the complexity to shoe horn another language into our code at 10% throughout gain." The W3 layer was deleted from claude/cluster-lookahead in full: the AssemblyScript kernels and their committed .wasm/.wat, the build script and the assemblyscript toolchain entry, the loader and the fixed-size linear-memory arena, the CENTAUR_WASM flag and its parser, the per-partition residency machinery, the differential suite, and the wasmRuns/wasmRefused engagement counters. The flag shipped `off`, so shipped behaviour is unchanged; the W2 packed-JS data layout that took partitionOf from 55 us to 26 us is a separate landed round and stays. P5R IS WITHDRAWN — there is no arm left to run it against, and the standing anomaly it existed to resolve is resolved by removal rather than by measurement: whatever the cap-rate cluster on headline-mix-king was, it can no longer be this flag. THIS IS THE ONE MOVE THE LADDER DOES NOT MAKE ON ITS OWN. Nothing in lib/ledger.js lets a measurement write a terminal status from `probe-passed`, and nothing should: the schema's seven statuses describe what evidence can do, and an owner ruling is not evidence, it is authority. The schema carries no owner-ruling or retired kind, so `frozen` is used as the closest terminal form the rules can express — CLOSED, moved by no p-value, re-opened only by a claim of a different kind — and the ruling is recorded here in the verdict text rather than forced into an invalid state. EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS THE HISTORICAL RECORD AND IS KEPT DELIBERATELY: the P5 cell is the exhibit that bought the ENGAGEMENT-TRISTATE refusal rule, and a rule whose exhibit has been deleted is a rule nobody can check. PRIOR VERDICT, 20260829, SUPERSEDED: THE ONE MEASURED ANOMALY ON THE BRANCH, AND IT IS STILL UNREADABLE. Placement is null on all three cells and that null is worth nothing: the arm cannot be shown to have run. Meanwhile four shape rows on the same cell say the games changed — twice the cap rate, ~21 more turns, ~22 more decisions, a quarter less decisive — and shape rows never move a status by rule, which is correct and is also exactly why this flag cannot be resolved from batch 1 at all. The root cause is already named upstream (refused per partition, silently; counters trapped in the module) and CL7 closed the telemetry, so the decisive experiment is now cheap and unambiguous. P5R IS THAT EXPERIMENT and it is the highest-value run in batch 2: it is the only scheduled experiment that resolves a standing anomaly rather than opening a new question, and its gate makes it impossible to mis-report — wasmRuns 0 on the treatment arm is a BROKEN ARM and must be reported as a refusal, not as a null. MACHINE INGEST, 20260829 — THE ANOMALY IS ONE ROW SMALLER AND ONE ROW SHARPER. The cap rate now has an interval of its own: +0.2292 [+0.0072, +0.4511] over 16 blocks against a MEASURED A/A floor of +/-0.2021, i.e. real but clearing the noise by 0.027. `null-snake6`'s 0.917 -> 1.000 saturation, which the fold listed as a corroborant, is INSIDE its floor (+0.0833 against +/-0.1100) and is withdrawn. `hazard-mix-king` is not a second instance: it churns 23 of 48 terminal kinds with a net of +1. The churn is ordinary for that cell; the 16-game swing is not. And the flipped games were SHORT (median 39.5 turns under wasm-off), with the subject +23.9 material ahead when the clock ran out — the shape is "cannot close out a won position", not "long games tip over the cap". Timing is identical to the millisecond per decision in both arms on all three cells, so the wall clock is not a back door to the engagement question. P5R remains the only instrument.

flags.verdict: Alive, unpromoted, and cheaper than it looked. It costs nothing measurable in placement (16 blocks against the pooled stratum's 58, so "no cost this cell could resolve"), it demonstrably runs, and on null-snake6 exhaustion deaths FALL under it (39 -> 33). What it has still never been shown to do is buy anything on its own. Note the asymmetry the batch settled: the cl-both arm reproduces the seed's collapse almost exactly (-0.573 vs -0.594; 72 deaths vs 75), so the cost in that pair is the seed's and not the pair's — but equally, the classifier is not a repair for the seed. MACHINE INGEST, 20260829: the "16 blocks against the pooled stratum's 58" reading is now contested by the batch's own dispersion. Computed from each cell's measured block SD instead of the pooled prior, 16 blocks resolves an MDE of 0.25 on all three cells (blocksNeeded 1, 3 and 8). That is true and it is not the question: the cost being looked for is two or three points, not twenty-five. P7F stays scheduled, and the rule that keeps it scheduled is now batch-scoped rather than reading whichever row was appended last — see MDE-HARDCODED and LIVE-NULL-IS-TERMINAL. Per-game rows also confirm the classifier is a near-exact no-op on unit loss: 53 -> 52 on null-snake6, 209 -> 209 on snake5-knight, and 48 of 48 teams alive at the end on the cell the seed destroys. SOURCE AND PER-GAME, 20260829 — NULL, AND SAFE TO PROMOTE ALONE. Three things the batch already contains, stated together for the first time: placement is NULL on every cell it ran; it PROVABLY ENGAGES (plans per decision +109.9 [+28.3, +191.5] ✱ on snake5-knight — a retired counter, quoted only as a broken-arm diagnostic, but it says the arm ran); and it is PROVABLY ORDER-PRESERVING — on null-snake6 it holds paired trajectory correlation at +0.912 with 45 of 48 games identical in length, against the A/A pair's 44 of 48, exactly as cl1-report.md's candidate-order test promises. Add exhaustion deaths FALLING under it on the two cells that matter (39 -> 33 on null-snake6, 16 -> 15 on headline-mix-king) and a near-exact no-op on total unit loss, and this flag should be taken forward ON ITS OWN EVIDENCE rather than as part of the cluster seed it was only ever entangled with by the cl-both arm. THE STATUS DOES NOT MOVE ON THIS PARAGRAPH AND MAY NOT: `supported` takes a supports-promotion row from a live paired sweep with a verified null AND engagement SHOWN by a counter, and batch 1 is structurally incapable of writing one — no 20260827 bundle carries the CL7 mechanism block (ENGAGEMENT-SOURCES). live-null stands and P7F stays scheduled; what changes is what P7F is FOR — a promotion experiment for a flag with a clean standalone safety case, not a rescue attempt for the seed.

Until the calibration lands, read this spec's PIECE cells (headline-mix-king, snake5-knight) under one rule: A DELTA ON A PIECE CELL IS QUOTED ONLY AGAINST N0's FLOOR MEASURED ON THAT SAME CELL, ON THE SAME BUNDLE, AT THE SAME BLOCK COUNT — and if that floor does not contain zero, the cell reports UNREADABLE and no verdict is written from it. The all-snake cells in this spec are unaffected and floor at +/-0.10. This is not a reason to skip the spec: its mechanism rows are per-decision counts, they are readable at this size, and they are what most of these experiments were designed to read.

nextExperiment.designNote: RESPECIFIED 20260830 AS A BRANCH-VERSUS-BRANCH VALIDATION, under the owner's branching ruling of the same day (docs/BRANCHING.md). THE ARMS ARE TWO BUNDLES FROM TWO REFS, both running their shipped defaults with no bot config on either side: `baseline` is built from origin/claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg, the validated baseline; `search-arch` is built from origin/claude/cluster-lookahead, the search-architecture feature branch, whose default bot carries the deep layer AND the cluster enumeration always-built. WHAT THIS DISSOLVES: the question this row carried until today was 'does the default bot keep carrying two never-raced features, or do they become config fields defaulting off until a sweep promotes them?'. Under the ruling there is no default to argue about — the accumulated architecture lives on a feature branch and the branch either MERGES on this evidence or it does not. The pending owner decision recorded on this row and on CENTAUR_CLUSTER_ENUM's is answered by the paradigm rather than by a status edit. WHAT IT COSTS, SAID OUT LOUD: the previous shape (`default` against `depthless` = bot={"depth":{"plyCap":0}}) was a one-variable pair — same bundle, same evaluator, same bounds, differing only in how far the search could look — and this one is not. Two branch tips differ by everything that landed on either since they forked, so a delta here attributes to THE BRANCH and to nothing finer. That is the correct instrument for a MERGE decision and the wrong one for a mechanism claim, and the two must not be confused in the write-up. The one-variable depth pair remains available on the feature bundle alone and is the follow-up if the branch arm reads positive and somebody wants to know which part of it did the work. AND READ THE RATE FOR WHAT IT IS: the 30% and 22.5% figures on the feature branch are DISAGREEMENT rates — how often removing depth would stage a different move — measured on 11x11 two-team piece boards. They are not improvement and they are not the owner's board; src/lobster/__tests__/DEPTH-NUMBERS.md is the committed record of what each figure measures, and the owner-shape rates (mixed-king 2/24, snake5-queen 5/24) are measured by the `depth-effect rate at the owner's shape` block of src/lobster/__tests__/depth-acceptance.test.ts. Their replay quality signal came back EMPTY — all seven disagreements replay identical same-turn ledgers — which is precisely why this live sweep is the instrument and the probes are not. nextExperiment.requires:
ONE BUNDLE PER ARM, BUILT FROM THE REF NAMED IN THE BUNDLES BLOCK, AND NO BOT CONFIG ON EITHER. The cross-branch shape is the harness's normal case, not an extension of it: build-bot.sh resolves any git ref to a bundle, and run-pair.js launches the arms at the same instant in separate processes and pairs them afterwards by gameId. Batch 1 ran exactly this shape in P1 — `integrated` @ 66904d2 against `perf-substrate` @ 8059b86, 144 games paired, 0 dropped, 0 pairing problems. DO NOT PASS bot= ON EITHER ARM. The baseline bundle predates the 20260829 flag teardown and has no src/lobster/bot-config module, so checkContenders would REFUSE the spec (correctly) the moment a contender declared one; with no bot config declared, nothing calls requireBundleTakesBotConfig and both arms simply play their shipped bots, which is the comparison this experiment is for. ENGAGEMENT IS READ ON THE search-arch ARM ONLY, from belief.deepestPlies / deepBranches on the per-game rows. The baseline arm is engagement-verified BY CONSTRUCTION — the deep layer is not in that build at all, so there is no counter to read and no silent-A/A risk on that side; the failure mode P5 taught (an arm that names a treatment and quietly does not run it) can only live on the search-arch side, which is where the gate below points.

MINIMUM BLOCKS FOR A CLAIMABLE READ: 73 PER CELL. Below that this spec is a DESCRIPTION, not a merge decision. At the emitted 16 blocks the expected half-width is 0.303 x sqrt(8/16) = about +/-0.21 sharePar, so a 16-block run may report only three things and must report them in these words: (1) THE ENGAGEMENT GATE below, which is a real pass/fail at any block count and is the single most valuable thing 16 blocks buys; (2) the mechanism rows — deepestPlies, deepBranches, depthEffectRate, worstWallMs, decisions — which are per-decision counts rather than per-game outcomes and are readable at this size; (3) a sharePar interval quoted WITH its half-width and labelled UNDERPOWERED FOR THE MERGE DECISION. A null at 16 blocks is NOT evidence the branch does not help and must never be written as one, because an effect of +0.2 sharePar would sit inside that interval. THE MERGE MAY NOT BE DECIDED — in either direction — ON A 16-BLOCK RUN. If the night has room for 73 blocks on even ONE cell, run the one cell at 73 rather than three cells at 16: one cell that can answer the question beats three that cannot.

MINIMUM BLOCKS FOR A CLAIMABLE READ ON A PIECE-BEARING CELL: 44, and this spec is emitted at 16. Blocks are a property of the SPEC and not of a cell (the standing CELL-QUALITY open item), so a piece cell cannot be raised without raising the all-snake cell beside it and the mandatory A/A null with it. Until the calibration lands, read this spec's PIECE cells (hazard-mix-king, headline-mix-king) under one rule: A DELTA ON A PIECE CELL IS QUOTED ONLY AGAINST N0's FLOOR MEASURED ON THAT SAME CELL, ON THE SAME BUNDLE, AT THE SAME BLOCK COUNT — and if that floor does not contain zero, the cell reports UNREADABLE and no verdict is written from it. The all-snake cells in this spec are unaffected and floor at +/-0.10. This is not a reason to skip the spec: its mechanism rows are per-decision counts, they are readable at this size, and they are what most of these experiments were designed to read.
nextExperiment.gate: deepestPlies > 0 and deepBranches > 0 on the `search-arch` arm, on at least the piece-bearing cells. ZERO THERE IS A BROKEN ARM AND MUST BE REPORTED AS A REFUSAL, NOT AS A NULL — it means the bundle was built from the wrong ref, or the deep layer never opened a thread on these boards, and either way the pair measured something other than what it is named for. Record the resolved SHA of both bundles from bundle.json in findings.md: a branch-versus-branch verdict that quotes branch names and not SHAs is a claim nobody can reproduce.
nextExperiment.mergeDecision: THIS EXPERIMENT IS THE MERGE DECISION FOR claude/cluster-lookahead. A `search-arch` arm that clears the verified A/A floor on the batch's own metrics merges into claude/mid-turn-collision-logic-mkxurg and is recorded VALIDATED. An arm that does not clear it does not merge; the branch stays a retained parallel test arm and the reason is written into findings.md. Neither outcome is a status word in this file's schema — the schema judges evidence about flags, and a branch merge is a judgement about a branch — so it is recorded here, in prose, where a reader meets it.
nextExperiment.power:
MEASURED, 20260830, AND IT SAYS 16 BLOCKS CANNOT SETTLE THIS. A sandbox preview ran exactly this pair — baseline 66904d2 against search-arch c74f0a1, both shipped defaults, 8 blocks, potions ON + hazard cross — and returned sharePar -0.01 [-0.31, +0.29]. THE ARM WAS NOT DEAD: 800 scout threads, 370 scout plies and 2,873 cluster joints per game, so the branch ran and decided differently. What it could not do is resolve. Cross-bundle paired spread was +/-0.303 at 8 blocks against an A/A floor of +/-0.10 on the same cells, i.e. THREE TIMES the floor, which cannot tell 'no effect' from 'an effect of 0.3' — the size that would decide the merge either way. Half-width scales as 1/sqrt(blocks), so the arithmetic is 8 x (0.303/0.10)^2 = 73 BLOCKS PER CELL = 219 games per arm per cell = 1,314 games for the spec. THIS SPEC IS EMITTED AT 16 BLOCKS ANYWAY, and that is a budget decision taken with the number in hand rather than an oversight — see REQUIRES for what 16 may and may not claim, and specs/batch2/README.md for what the alternative costs. The 73 is a floor on the blocks, not a target: it buys +/-0.10, which is the smallest effect this instrument can see at all.

PIECE-BEARING CELLS ARE NOT SIZED BY THIS SPEC'S BLOCK COUNT — MEASURED 20260830. An A/A null on a piece-bearing cell, potions ON + hazard cross, TWO IDENTICAL BUNDLES with identical configs and identical seeds, returned sharePar +0.271 [0.037, 0.506] at 8 blocks. IT EXCLUDES ZERO. A cell whose null excludes zero has no floor, and a treatment delta with no floor is UNREADABLE rather than null — the ledger's own rule. All-snake cells at the same size floored cleanly at +/-0.10 (measurements: snakes potions-off +0.041 +/- 0.097, snakes potions-ON hazard -0.093 +/- 0.159 and -0.064 +/- 0.099, against queen potions-ON hazard +0.053 +/- 0.120 on one bundle and +0.271 +/- 0.234 on the other). Carrying the widest measured piece-cell half-width forward, +/-0.234 at 8 blocks, the arithmetic for a +/-0.10 floor is 8 x (0.234/0.10)^2 = 44 BLOCKS PER PIECE CELL. THE CROSSOVER HAS NOT BEEN MEASURED and 44 is an extrapolation from one point, which is why batch 3's rank-2 item is the calibration run that measures it (A/A pairs at 8/16/32/64 blocks on one piece cell, both bundles) rather than a guess repeated at owner-shape prices.

That gap between what the ledger says a feature has earned and what the shipped bot does is the finding, and closing it by editing a status here would be the ledger promoting something no sweep promoted. P11 is respecified as that branch-versus-branch arm and is the merge decision. Over 180 randomly sampled batch-1 games (18,371 turn-boards, 181,512 unit-observations), TeamDetector.getTeamKey (src/logic/team-detector.ts) agrees with ground-truth `teamID` on every single observation — flip rate 0.000000, with `teamID` present and non-empty everywhere — so every batch-1 death attribution that depends on team identity, including the DEATH-CAUSE-SINGLE-KEY close, is safe. Counterfactually stripping teamID, 18,371 of 18,371 boards (100%) resolve to a different number of teams — all 18 units collapse into one. Worth a fixture assertion that `teamID` is present on every unit, rather than a code change; the precedence is right and team-detector.ts:32-37 already records that the fallbacks exist for legacy HTTP-era logs. openInstrumentItems.what: bin/ingest.js decides a verdict by SIGN ALONE: a mechanism or placement delta outside the null band scores `failed` if its mean is negative and `supports-promotion` if positive. It has no notion of which metrics are better when they go DOWN. So deathsExhaustion, deathsSelf, fatalStagings, teammateKills, place, boundsInversions, overrunRate and every other cost-shaped counter are scored exactly backwards.
openInstrumentItems.impact: SEVERE, AND THE EXHIBIT IS THIS LEDGER`S FOUNDING FINDING. CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED's failure is an exhaustion-death INCREASE of +36 per 48 games on a metric declared family:mechanism. Run through the ingest, that positive delta scores `supports-promotion`. It is caught here only because the flag is ALREADY live-failed and "a supporting cell does not overturn a live failure" refuses it — i.e. the ledger is saved by a different rule, and would not have been had the flag still been probe-passed when the row arrived. Two further rows in the batch-1 fold trip it in the other direction: UNIT_FATALITY's exhaustion deaths FALLING 39 -> 33 would score `failed`, and TERRITORY_SLIDER_PROFILE's place improving by -0.229 would score `failed`. All three are recorded by hand with the correct verdict and a polarity note.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: The fold declares `lowerIsBetter: true` on the affected promotionMetrics entries of CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED and CENTAUR_UNIT_FATALITY. Nothing reads the field yet. It exists so the fix is a lookup rather than a re-derivation.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: A one-line change on claude/cluster-lookahead, in bin/ingest.js's verdict expression: consult the gate's `lowerIsBetter` and flip the sign test. Plus the polarity declarations on the remaining gate metrics, and a selftest assertion that a falling death count does not read as a failure. NOT applied here: this branch is the mirror and its code must not fork from home.

openInstrumentItems.what: applyMeasurement has no concept of a CONTROL cell. A cell that is null BY DESIGN — a provably-inert path included precisely to prove the instrument reports zero when zero is the truth — is indistinguishable to the rules from a treatment cell that failed to show an effect, and it takes the same `live-null` branch.
openInstrumentItems.impact: Demonstrated live during the batch-1 fold. TERRITORY_SLIDER_PROFILE's null-snake6 control sat at EXACTLY 0 against a measured +/-0.0324 floor — the strongest single row in the ledger, because it shows the measurement is not manufacturing effects — and filing it as family `placement` demoted the flag `supported` -> `live-null`. The better the control, the harder it demotes. This is a rule that punishes the practice it exists to encourage.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: The row is filed as family `audit`, which never moves a status and is arguably its true family anyway: an inert control is evidence about the INSTRUMENT, not a placement claim about the treatment. Recorded on the row itself so the choice is not mistaken for a dodge.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: On claude/cluster-lookahead: an explicit `control: true` on a measurement, refused from moving a status and rendered as a distinct badge; plus a selftest asserting that a passing control does not demote a supported flag. Until then `audit` is the correct filing and the note carries the reasoning.
openInstrumentItems.closedIn: CLOSED. `control` is a fourth measurement kind. It enters no effect channel in either direction and accumulates on the flag`s `controlEvidence`; a control that MOVES is recorded under `violated` as an instrument failure, because a path required to read zero reading nonzero makes every treatment row beside it provisional. The slider`s row is re-filed as placement/control and no longer demotes; the selftest keeps the defect reachable by asserting that the SAME row filed as a placement null still demotes, so the fix is the kind and not a loosening of the null rule. cl/llfix on claude/cluster-lookahead — see lib/polarity.js, lib/ledger.js MEASUREMENT_KINDS, and bin/selftest.js sections 1b / 4.

openInstrumentItems.what: ingest.js can read engagement from exactly one place: `health[].mechanism[<counter>]`, the CL7 block. No bundle built before CL7 has it, so `--engagement` returns `null` = CANNOT SAY on every arm of every pre-CL7 batch, and the ENGAGEMENT-TRISTATE rule then moves nothing. The consequence is total, not marginal: NO pre-CL7 batch can write a live status through the machine path, whatever it measured. AND THE SILENT REFUSAL NOW HAS AN ADDRESS (20260829, source-level at 8059b86): `territory.ts:388-416` runs an ALL-OR-NOTHING residency check — a single `-1` pointer, including one from a loop over every entry's `entEarliest[e]`, sends the WHOLE partition back to JS — against a FIXED-SIZE arena (`arena.ts`: memory is created with `initial === maximum`, and `alloc*` returns null when it is full), sized from a measured working set that a larger or slider-heavy roster overflows. That is the mechanism by which an arm can genuinely run and still read as not-engaged, it is the best available explanation for why the piece cells show less than the snake cell, and it converts "wasm may be refused on piece boards" into an arena-sizing bug with a file and a line. The check returns a bare `false` from ~8 distinct pointer tests, so P5R should log WHICH buffer was non-resident and by how much the arena was over.
openInstrumentItems.exhibit: CENTAUR_CLUSTER_SEED lost snake6 1.00 -> 0.15, 13-18x the measured floor, with plansEvaluated roughly doubling and 27 of 48 games ending in the subject's elimination where the off arm never lost a team. An arm that did not engage cannot do that. The ledger already accepts exactly this kind of reasoning -- CENTAUR_COHORT_POLICY carries an `engagementEvidence` block built from worstWallMs and the retired plansEvaluated as a broken-arm diagnostic -- but the ingest has no channel to supply it.
openInstrumentItems.workaround: NONE TAKEN, DELIBERATELY. Passing a counter that does not exist, or asserting engagement on the command line, would bend the datum to fit the code -- the exact move ENGAGEMENT-TRISTATE was raised to retire. The machine wrote `null` and moved nothing, and the hand-adjudicated statuses stand on their own record.
openInstrumentItems.closedBy: a decision that is the owner's, not the loop's: either a second engagement channel (--engagement-evidence <metric> <arm-delta>, admitting a broken-arm diagnostic as evidence of running), or the acceptance that pre-CL7 batches are informative and never status-moving, in which case every row above is correctly refused and P5R/P7R are the only paths. NOT DECIDED HERE.

openInstrumentItems.what: THE LEDGER HAS NOWHERE TO RECORD HOW MUCH A CELL CAN MEASURE, so no rule can refuse a row for being asked on a board that cannot answer it. `headline-mix-king` — the batch's headline board, and the cell the wasm anomaly is reported on — is trajectory-unstable under ZERO treatment: the A/A null flips 26 of 48 placements between two builds of the SAME commit (54%), only 5 of 48 games come out identical, the paired turn-correlation is -0.193, A/A plans-per-decision swings +65%, and across 14 arm-sweeps of the identical configHash 3749a5dea5e82e99 the cap rate spans 0.229-0.458 (mean 0.306, sd 0.060) — batch 1's two wasm arms being exactly the minimum and the maximum of that spread. Pairing by seed buys NO variance reduction there. THE DESIGN QUESTION, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ITEM IS FOR AND ALL IT IS FOR: where should cell quality LIVE so that rules can consume it — a block on the batch record, a field on the A/A null's own rows, or a table the ingest derives and the generator reads — and WHICH RULES should it feed: refuse a placement verdict outright, require a larger n, or disqualify the cell from a spec at generation time? NOT DECIDED HERE, AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT. No `batches[].cellQuality` machinery was invented for it: the schema should follow the decision rather than lead it, and inventing a channel now would commit the loop to whichever of the three shapes happened to be easiest to write.

standingExperiments.title: The budget ladder
standingExperiments.approvedBy: owner — pre-approved, conditional on budget-probe v2 confirming
standingExperiments.trigger: CONFIRMED, and here is the whole arithmetic. budget-probe v2, 60 recorded positions drawn from 480 integrated replays, idle box, FRESH ENGINE PER POSITION, sample seed 1, 9 skipped: a true 1000 ms run reproduces the 2000 ms decision on 55 of 60 positions. FLIPS 5/60 = 8.3% (+/-7.0). A/A FLOOR, 2000 ms against itself: 1/60 = 1.7% (+/-3.2). EXCESS ATTRIBUTABLE TO BUDGET = 6.7 points, wide at n=60 and the intervals overlap — the direction is clear and the magnitude is not. The condition on the owner's pre-approval is met.
standingExperiments.question: Where on the budget curve does the substrate stop being speed and start being strength? P1 found the perf substrate was speed-not-strength at 2000 ms; the bimodal revision result (65% of decisions settle by 250 ms, 34.8% revise in a wave at 1000-1500 ms, nothing between) says 1000 ms would amputate the second pass entirely. Three points draw the line.
standingExperiments.designNote: ONE trail-instrumented cell in the ladder. The 35% revision wave was measured PRE-CL3, and cluster enumeration front-loads coordination, so the wave's own shape may have moved — which would make the ladder's middle rung mean something different from what it meant last month. Mechanism-first at 8 blocks: placement is descriptive here, not claimable. BATCH-1 NOTE: the 500 ms rung is now the interesting one. If the deep pass lands at 1000-1500 ms and the engine reschedules it under a 1 s budget, then 1000 ms may barely differ from 2000 ms while 500 ms amputates the pass outright — so the ladder's information is concentrated at its bottom rung.
standingExperiments.caveat: CHANGED != IMPROVED, and nothing measures the difference. The 35.0%/60.1% figures count decisions whose staged move-set changed; the 8.3% counts decisions a shorter budget decides differently. Whether those ~7% are BETTER is unmeasured and is exactly what the ladder is for.
standingExperiments.reconciliation: TWO INSTRUMENTS THAT LOOK LIKE THEY DISAGREE, AND DO NOT. The emission trails say 35.0% (P4, 50,455 decisions) and 60.1% (P5, 52,191) of decisions differ from what was staged at 1000 ms. budget-probe v2 says a true 1 s budget reproduces the 2 s decision 91.7% of the time. Both are right. The last-emission histogram shows the engine stages an incumbent in under 250 ms in 99.9% of decisions and then either never revises or revises in a single wave landing at 1000-1500 ms — the 250-1000 ms window is EMPTY, 8 decisions out of 102,646. The engine is deadline-aware: under a 1 s budget it RESCHEDULES the deep pass rather than losing it. So "what was on the table at 1000 ms" and "what a 1000 ms engine decides" are different questions, and only the second is the one the ladder asks. Net: the second second changes about 7% of decisions.
standingExperiments.retracted: budget-probe v1 IS RETRACTED — DO NOT INGEST. It reused one engine across games, and engines carry per-game ledger state, so its results were degenerate (0/60 flips in 26 s). Fixed in 65aa973. If a v1 file turns up in the archive, it is not evidence.
standingExperiments.power: PIECE-BEARING CELLS ARE NOT SIZED BY THIS SPEC'S BLOCK COUNT — MEASURED 20260830. An A/A null on a piece-bearing cell, potions ON + hazard cross, TWO IDENTICAL BUNDLES with identical configs and identical seeds, returned sharePar +0.271 [0.037, 0.506] at 8 blocks. IT EXCLUDES ZERO. A cell whose null excludes zero has no floor, and a treatment delta with no floor is UNREADABLE rather than null — the ledger's own rule. All-snake cells at the same size floored cleanly at +/-0.10 (measurements: snakes potions-off +0.041 +/- 0.097, snakes potions-ON hazard -0.093 +/- 0.159 and -0.064 +/- 0.099, against queen potions-ON hazard +0.053 +/- 0.120 on one bundle and +0.271 +/- 0.234 on the other). Carrying the widest measured piece-cell half-width forward, +/-0.234 at 8 blocks, the arithmetic for a +/-0.10 floor is 8 x (0.234/0.10)^2 = 44 BLOCKS PER PIECE CELL. THE CROSSOVER HAS NOT BEEN MEASURED and 44 is an extrapolation from one point, which is why batch 3's rank-2 item is the calibration run that measures it (A/A pairs at 8/16/32/64 blocks on one piece cell, both bundles) rather than a guess repeated at owner-shape prices.
standingExperiments.requires: MINIMUM BLOCKS FOR A CLAIMABLE READ ON A PIECE-BEARING CELL: 44, and this spec is emitted at 8. Blocks are a property of the SPEC and not of a cell (the standing CELL-QUALITY open item), so a piece cell cannot be raised without raising the all-snake cell beside it and the mandatory A/A null with it. Until the calibration lands, read this spec's PIECE cells (headline-mix-king) under one rule: A DELTA ON A PIECE CELL IS QUOTED ONLY AGAINST N0's FLOOR MEASURED ON THAT SAME CELL, ON THE SAME BUNDLE, AT THE SAME BLOCK COUNT — and if that floor does not contain zero, the cell reports UNREADABLE and no verdict is written from it. The all-snake cells in this spec are unaffected and floor at +/-0.10. This is not a reason to skip the spec: its mechanism rows are per-decision counts, they are readable at this size, and they are what most of these experiments were designed to read.
